clock_meridiem_am: Hausa scopes a clock reading with a following na-phrase naming the part of
the day.  Each band below is fixed by a worked example on
ha.wikipedia.org where the article's own text or its parenthetical
"ƙarfe 7:59 na safiyar ranar sha ɗaya" is the 07:59 departure of the first
aircraft on 11 September, and "ƙarfe 09:00 na safiyar Litinin" is 09:00.
safe and safiya are the same word's two shapes.
clock_meridiem_night: Hausa scopes a clock reading with a following na-phrase naming the part of
the day.  Each band below is fixed by a worked example on
ha.wikipedia.org where the article's own text or its parenthetical
na dare is a midnight-crossing band, not a uniform twelve-hour shift.
ha.wikipedia.org writes "ƙarfe 2 na dare" for a death in the small hours
and "ƙarfe 1:00 na dare" for a night raid, but "ƙarfe 9:05 na dare" and
"ƙarfe 11:30 na dare" for the late evening.  The resolver's band split --
hours one to five stay morning, six to eleven become evening, twelve is
clock_meridiem_pm: Hausa scopes a clock reading with a following na-phrase naming the part of
the day.  Each band below is fixed by a worked example on
ha.wikipedia.org where the article's own text or its parenthetical
"ƙarfe 1:00 na rana (12:00 GMT)" is 13:00 -- Nigeria runs an hour ahead of
GMT, so the parenthetical conversion fixes na rana as the afternoon.
"daga ƙarfe 7:30 zuwa 11:30 na safe, sai kuma 2:30 zuwa 6:00 na yamma" is a
school day running 07:30-11:30 and again 14:30-18:00, which fixes na yamma
marker_and: da joins the bounds of a between-frame ("tsakanin X da Y") and, inside a
numeral, joins each component to the next ("ashirin da biyar" = 25;
ha.wikipedia.org, which glosses its own spelled numerals with digits).
marker_between: tsakanin X da Y.  Attested in temporal use on ha.wikipedia.org: "tsakanin
marker_day_word: The day noun opening a date line -- "ranar 5 ga Yuli, 2021"
marker_every: The distributive determiner, in both genders: "kowace Litinin", "kowane
marker_from: The opening half of a range, closed by zuwa.  Attested on ha.wikipedia.org:
"daga Asabar zuwa laraba", "ƙarfe 7:30 zuwa 11:30 na safe".
marker_future: Every future relativeTime pattern is "cikin <unit> {0}" or "a cikin <unit>
{0}" -- literally "inside", leading the unit it counts.
bayan is the ordinary "after", and "bayan kwanaki hudu" (ha.wikipedia.org)
is the same forward offset cikin names, so it reads as one too.
marker_ga: ga stands between the day number and the month name in the ordinary Hausa
date line: "10 ga watan Oktoba 2022", "26 ga Janairu, 1981",
"21 ga watan Afrilu" (ha.wikipedia.org).  CLDR's date patterns omit it.
marker_last: relative-type--1: "watan da ya gabata", "satin da ya gabata", "Laraba da
ta gabata", "Asabar da ta wuce".  The marker trails its noun and is the
same relative clause the counted past uses, so last-week and N-weeks-ago
marker_month_word: The month noun standing before a month name -- "watan Oktoba 2022"
marker_next: relative-type-1: "sati na gaba" / "wata na gaba", the week or month ahead.
CLDR's weekday form "Laraba mai zuwa" (the coming Wednesday) is the other
half of the field and is deliberately NOT shipped: it ends in zuwa, which is
also this locale's range terminator ("daga Litinin zuwa Jumaʼa"), and the
range split reads the raw token stream before multiword surfaces are glued
back together.  Shipping it would let "Litinin mai zuwa" be read as the open
range "up to Monday" -- a wrong answer rather than no answer -- so the
surface stays out until the two can be told apart.
marker_oclock: ƙarfe introduces the hour of the day and leads its number: "ƙarfe 7:45 na
dare", "ƙarfe 2 na rana".  Written Hausa spells the hooked ƙ as a plain k
about as often as not, so karfe ships beside it.
marker_of: The genitive linker, masculine na and feminine ta: "sati na gaba",
marker_past: Every past relativeTime pattern is the unit, the count, and a trailing
relative clause: "kwanaki {0} da suka gabata", "wata {0} da ya gabata",
"shekara {0} da ta gabata".  The verb agrees with the unit noun -- ya for
masculine, ta for feminine, suka for the plural -- so all three ship: which
one is grammatical was settled by the noun the writer already chose.
CLDR gives wuce beside gabata for Friday and Saturday; the two verbs are
interchangeable in the frame and both ship.
marker_since: tun opens a stretch reaching back from a point already gone; it is the
word written before daga in "tun daga watan Fabrairun 2024"
marker_this: relative-type-0: "wannan satin", "wannan Litinin".  Unlike the other
relative markers this one leads its noun.

marker_year_plural: The plural of "shekara" (year).  A count of years takes the plural

marker_year_word: The year noun standing before its number -- "shekara ta 1926", "shekarar

month_2: CLDR spells February Faburairu; Nigerian written Hausa overwhelmingly
writes Fabrairu, and both spellings ship because both are attested.
The linked form is the genitive that a month name takes inside the date
line ("watan faburairu 2027"); harvested from ha.wikipedia.org by a corpus
count over the frame "watan <month>" (Fabrairu 12 / Fabrairun 8 / Faburairu 1).
month_3: Maris ends in a consonant and takes no -n linker: the corpus frame
"watan Maris" returns the bare name in every hit.
month_4: CLDR spells April Afirilu, written usage prefers Afrilu; both ship.
The linked form is the genitive that a month name takes inside the date

count over the frame "watan <month>" (Afrilu 11 / Afrilun 9 / Afirilu 6 / Afirilun 4).

named_day_-2: CLDR carries no relative-type--2 for Hausa.  shekaranjiya is glossed
"day-before-yesterday" in two independent Chadic comparative wordlists on
ha.wikipedia.org (the Polci and Geranci articles), which is the attestation
this file rests on.  There is no relative-type-2 counterpart: no source
consulted attests a day-after-tomorrow word, so none ships.
unit_hour: hour displayName awa, plural awanni.  Hausa reckons the hour of the day on
the Western clock (see clock_meridiem_pm.voc), so unlike the Swahili saa
this noun carries no competing traditional count.
unit_minute: minute displayName minti, plural mintuna; mintin is the definite form of
unit_month: month displayName wata, plural watanni.  watan is the linked form the
relativeTime pattern uses ("a cikin watan {0}") and the form that stands
before a month name in the date line.
unit_second: second displayName daƙiƙa; the relativeTime patterns spell the same word
dakika in the singular and dakiku in the plural, without the hooked ƙ.
All three surfaces are CLDR's own and all three ship.
unit_week: week displayName mako, plural makonni.  sati is CLDR's own second word for
a week -- it is what relative-type--1 ("satin da ya gabata") and
relativePeriod ("sati na {0}") are built on -- and en.wiktionary.org gives
the two as synonyms.  satin is the definite form CLDR itself writes in
unit_year: year displayName shekara, plural shekaru; shekarar is the linked form
weekday_4: ca-gregorian spells Friday Jummaʼa with a doubled m, dateFields spells
it Jumaʼa; the two CLDR files disagree, so both ship.  The modifier
apostrophe U+02BC folds to a plain apostrophe in the tokenizer.
weekday_abbr_0: days.format.abbreviated.  An abbreviation binds a marker-ed order but
never a bare weekday, so a three-letter form cannot claim a span on its
own.  The two-letter days.format.short series (Li, Ta, Lr, Al, Ju, As,
Lh) is deliberately not shipped: Ta collides with the feminine genitive
linker and the rest are equally ordinary letter pairs.
